commit.message:
validation-gen: add a worked custom-prefix example

Add examples/custom-prefix: a complete generator for a hypothetical project
whose tags use "+xyz:", with a tag of its own (+xyz:startsWith) backed by a
validation function outside apimachinery. Its layout mirrors what a
third-party module would contain, so it doubles as the template to copy and
as a regression test that the standard tags work under another prefix.

The output_tests packages follow the same pattern as validation-gen's own:
doc.go declares tagged types, go:generate runs the generator, and doc_test.go
asserts the resulting field.ErrorList through the testscheme.

hack/update-codegen.sh regenerates the example, since the repo-wide tag
search does not find "+xyz:" packages and the cleanup pass would otherwise
delete its output without restoring it.

commit.message:
validation-gen: make the tag prefix configurable

Every tag validation-gen reads was hard-coded with the "k8s:" prefix, so a
third-party project using this generator had to annotate its API types with
Kubernetes' own tag names.

Make the prefix a parameter. A TagValidator now returns its name relative to
the prefix ("required", not "k8s:required"), and the registry qualifies it
when InitGlobalValidator is called. Registration is deferred until then, so
the prefix is known before any name is formed. Validators that name other
tags, in messages or when inspecting a nested tag value, get the prefix via
Config.TagPrefix. The generator's own package-level tags (validation-gen,
validation-gen-scheme-registry, ...) follow the same prefix through the new
apidefinitions.ValidationSpec, as do the tags the lint rules look for.

--tag-prefix sets it, defaulting to "k8s:". Kubernetes' own generated code
and --docs output are unchanged.

commit.message:
validation-gen: split the generator into importable packages

validation-gen was a single main package, so nothing in it could be
imported. A project that wants this generator with its own tags, or with
a different tag prefix, has to be able to build its own binary on the
same code.

Move the generator into k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/generators
and its flags into .../args, matching the layout of defaulter-gen and
conversion-gen. printDocs becomes generators.PrintDocs, which writes to an
io.Writer instead of stdout. main.go is now just flag parsing and a call to
gengo.Execute.

No behavior change: the generated output and --docs output are byte
identical, modulo the trailing newline that fmt.Println added to --docs.
